day1.note: baseline variance parts on the first forecast day; t_days = days since the last dip; the overview's gap band is the same noise term from t = 0 on the dip to t = age on the day before this one

forecast.variance_note: pooled decomposition over the realisations (diagnostic); the realisation share is not in the band; noise = sigma2 x noise_inflation^2 x (1 - exp(-2 (lead + age) / tau)), noise_inflation the site's hindcast factor on the noise sd (config/fit_anchors, 1 when not estimated)

reference.note: APA / SNIRH reference levels: for each calendar month, the 20th percentile and the median of every qc-pass SNIRH dip taken in that month over the whole record. A level below the month's P20 is the driest fifth of what that month has held, between P20 and the median the lower half, above the median the upper half. Months with fewer than 5 dips carry no thresholds. The whole record is one sample, so a well whose levels have trended carries that trend inside its own reference.

reference_status.note: months of the hydrological year (1 October) to the end of the forecast horizon, each against the P20 and median of its own calendar month. A month with measurements carries their mean; a month without one carries the model - on the observed weather before the issue date, on the weather members after it - which is model output, not a measurement. The months between the last measurement and the issue date are modelled like the rest.

anchor.refit: kept (0 new dips since 2026-06-29, anchor 17 d old)

realisations.mode: baseline_only (diagnostic: 5 realisations pooled for the variance share)
realisations.evidence: hindcast 2026-09-05 (revised fits), esp_real vs esp at anchor age 0: trajectory CRPSS 0.147 vs 0.387, coverage90 0.959 vs 0.923; season end CRPSS -0.004 vs 0.239, coverage90 0.955 vs 0.905 (first pass: 0.153 vs 0.367, 0.952 vs 0.892; 0.037 vs 0.245, 0.94 vs 0.879)

dips.note: qc-pass SNIRH dips; residual_m = dip - simulation, null before the calibration start; apa_class is the dip against the P20 and median of its own calendar month (`reference`)

simulation.note: simulation on the observed forcing (gap-filled after observed_to) with the parameters used for the forecast; no residual correction

corrected.note: simulation + anchor residual decayed with tau from the last dip; the forecast median continues from its last value

members.note: weather members only: for each spliced EC46/SEAS5 member, the head path averaged over the parameter samples with the anchor residual decayed as in the median, so the members continue from the corrected path. The parameter and noise spread is in the forecast bands (p05..p95), not in these paths.

pumping.formulation_text: Pumping as negative recharge: m = 6 on the footprint-modulated irrigation demand
pumping.series: prec_net = prec_mm - (6 x irrig_cwb_mm x rs_level (the share the stress table carries) + 6 x ada_m3d as a depth over 319.7 km2)
pumping.note: pumping as negative recharge: the recharge model's precipitation is prec_net = P - [m x crop-water-balance irrigation draw at the inferred share x L + m_a x public supply as a depth over the domain + beta x all-parcel demand x drought indicator]; L is the footprint level (the remote-sensing extent index over its 2022-2024 mean, 1.0 over any horizon; 1 with level constant), m_a the AdA weight (m by default), the switch term extra pumping when the Arade storage or the 24-month rain is in deficit (absent without a switch); the pumping shares the recharge response and gain; m, the level, m_a and the switch are chosen per site by the split-sample rule over grids, so the spatial concentration of the wells and the level of the inferred share are folded into m, which also trades against the ET factor, and the response carries no delay beyond the recharge response. The head effect is the effective pumping through the response: the mean drawdown and the mean yearly peak over effect_years.

config.shift_rule: the bias is fitted on the standardised error, so the shift in metres is z_bias x the band's own standard deviation on the day: near zero on the first horizon day and largest at the season end
config.target_rule: the season-end target of the drawdown season, 1 April + 183 days; the coefficient vector is the linear interpolation in issue date between the two bracketing nodes and the zero vector on the target day
config.not_applied: the east (the correction gains nothing there: 1 Apr season-end CRPSS 0.540 -> 0.531 leave-one-year-out), 596/259 (sector `uncertain`: one well, so a per-sector fit does no pooling - below MIN_NODE_SITES = 2; its leave-one-year-out fit gained +0.099 at 1 April and is an open item, not a product form), a 1 October issue (0.325 -> 0.260, it loses), any date before 1 April or at and after the season-end target

scenarios.formulation_text: Pumping as negative recharge: m = 6 on the footprint-modulated irrigation demand

floor.label: reporting floor: the share that reproduces the 2024 and 2025 reported irrigation totals

inferred.label: M5 inferred: reported titles + IFAP duty of the non-reporting titles (42.64 hm3 in 2025) as a share of the model's 2025 all-parcel gross

baseline.label: calendar-month climatology of the last 36 reported months (2023-06 to 2026-05)

drought.label: the highest 12-month public-supply draw on record (2019-08 to 2020-07, 2019/20) with the same monthly shape

scenarios.note: irrigation level x AdA level; the irrigation share rescales the crop-water-balance draw (and the proxy by share / floor share), the AdA level replaces the public-supply series over the horizon; the default run is the published band (forecast.*, daily). Bands differ across scenarios only through the model's pumping term (net pumping, m = 6: prec_net = P - m x pump_mm). The irrigation level rescales the crop-water-balance part (footprint level 1.0 over the horizon), the AdA level the public-supply series (weight 6).
